dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Hi, yes, good morning, or I guess it's almost noon now. This is Jorge Spencer. So, I should say, I almost didn't pick up, because I get dozens of spam calls a day on this phone, like car warranty, the whole list. But I saw it was a local number, so I answered the callback, or, well, I'm the one calling you, but I had missed a call from this exchange earlier and I figured I'd better try.
Okay, no problem. I'm not sure who called you from here, but I'm glad you reached us. What can I do for you, Mr. Spencer?

Right, right. So I rent, I've been in the apartment about two years now, and the landlord told me when I moved in that the trash goes out Thursdays, and recycling is every other week. And I have a Christmas tree, a real one, we got it over the weekend, and I want to know about the Christmas tree pickup. Like when it happens and how to put it out.
Sure. Let me just get your address so I can look at your route. What's the address?
It's 126 Washington Street, in the Point.
One twenty-six Washington Street. Okay, give me a second. [pause] Alright, so are you asking about the tree because you've had a pickup that didn't happen, or you're just planning ahead?

Little of both. Last week, the trash was out by the curb by seven, I always do it the night before, and nobody took it. And the week before that, same thing, they skipped us. So that's the second miss in a row. I figured maybe the schedule changed for the holidays and I missed a notice, and then I thought, well, if I'm calling about that I might as well ask about the tree.
Okay, so two Thursdays in a row your trash wasn't picked up at one twenty-six Washington. Let me make a note of that. Was it the bags, or a bin?
A bin, the city bin, the green one. Lid closed, the handle facing the street, like the sheet says.

Good. Alright. I'll put in a missed pickup report for you. And for the tree, the holiday tree collection usually runs in early January, after the holidays, and it's separate from your regular trash. You'd put it at the curb with no bag, no stand, no lights or tinsel on it. I don't have the exact dates in front of me for this year, so I'd rather you check the city's collection notice, or I can have someone call you back with the dates.
Okay, so not before Christmas, it's after. And no bag. I was going to put it in one of those tree bags so the needles don't get everywhere.
Right, I'd skip the bag. Bagged trees often get left behind. Just set it loose at the curb.
Got it. And with the rain coming today, the soaker, should I wait on putting the bin out tomorrow, or just do it like normal?

Put it out like normal, tomorrow morning or tonight, whatever you usually do. If the weather's bad they may run late, but they'd still come by. If it's not picked up by the end of the day Thursday, call us back.
Okay. And you have my address for the missed pickups, one twenty-six Washington.
I do. Let me read it back. Jorge Spencer, one twenty-six Washington Street, missed trash pickup two weeks running, green city bin. Do you want a call back with the tree dates? What's a good number?
Yeah, it's 401-555-0157. And if it's a number I don't know, I'll try to pick up, but no promises, with the spam.
Understood. I'll note to leave a voicemail. 401-555-0157, right?
That's it. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Mr. Spencer. Stay dry out there.
